conviction_note: The findings sum to +0.3: a peer and industry RevPAR read-through and a crowded short against a Street bar already above the top of guidance and a peer group that sold its own RevPAR beats in the same fortnight. Both measurements give a small positive lean (p_up 53 on a 6% absolute move, +0.36). The sizes are small because the read-through is a proxy and was partly priced by the +8.5% 20-day run-up, not because the move will be small.
bar: Q3 adj EPS consensus $2.26 (Earnings Whispers preview, 2026-10-26, whisper $2.23: https://finviz.com/news/407869/choice-hotels-faces-a-q3-test-of-its-rebound-as-the-street-prices-above-guidance) and $2.28 at Benzinga. Revenue consensus $449.3M (Benzinga) to $454.9M (EW). The two EPS sources agree within $0.02. Company guide (8-K 2026-08-05, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001046311/000104631126000023/exhibit991earningspressrel.htm): FY26 adj EPS $6.86-7.10, adj EBITDA $635-650M, US RevPAR 0% to +1.25%. On the Q2 call the company said Q3 US RevPAR would 'exceed second quarter levels' (Q2 was +1.3%) and then moderate in Q4. FY consensus EPS of $7.14 already sits above the top of the guide. Q3 2025 comparison: adj EPS $2.10, US RevPAR -3.2%, and about $9.5M of non-recurring liquidated damages.
positioning_check: Short interest 6.33M shares as of 2026-10-15, 12.8 days to cover, about 14% of the 45.0M shares outstanding (https://massive.com/quote/chh, read 2026-10-30). Equibles shows about 16% of float. The free float is smaller than shares outstanding because the founding family holds a large stake, so this is a crowded short. 25d skew is null in the baseline. Put/call OI ratio is 4.79, but total OI is only 139 contracts, and the ATM spread is 68% of mid, so the 5.53% implied move is indicative only. Run-up: +8.46% over 20 days, +2.48% over 5 days, 8.9% below the 52-week high.

findings.finding: Peer and industry read-through says CHH's Q3 US RevPAR probably beats its own framing ('above Q2's +1.3%'). Wyndham, the closest economy/midscale franchisor, printed Q3 2026 US RevPAR +6% on 2026-10-21 against -5% in Q3 2025 (two-year stack about +0.7%). CHH's Q3 2025 comparison was -3.2%, so the same two-year stack implies roughly +4% for CHH. Hilton printed US RevPAR +7%. STR's industry series ran July +8.2%, August +2.0%, and +10.4% and +14.2% in the last two September weeks. The offset: CHH said the World Cup gave it only 'limited' Q3 exposure, while Wyndham credited a favorable World Cup impact.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 (2026-08-05): US RevPAR +1.3% with a raised RevPAR/EBITDA guide bought +2.93%. Q3 2025 (US RevPAR -3.2%, guide cut) still bought +5.98%. Q1 2026, an adj EPS miss with a steady outlook, fell -15.58%. The stock reacts to EPS and guidance more than to RevPAR.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced. CHH ran from $103.44 (Oct 14) to $113.66 (Oct 21) into Wyndham's print, and FY consensus EPS of $7.14 already sits above the guide top. If the full +4% were priced, Q3 consensus would sit well above the company's '>1.3%' framing, and the EW whisper ($2.23) would not sit below consensus ($2.26). The whisper below consensus suggests it is not fully priced.

findings.finding: The Street already models a guidance raise. FY26 consensus adj EPS of $7.14 sits above the top of the company's $6.86-7.10 range, which was lowered on 2026-08-05 for higher interest expense and a 26% tax rate. A RevPAR raise that leaves EPS guidance at or near $7.10 would read as a miss against the bar. Hilton also flagged Q4 headwinds (US midterm elections, the Middle East), while Wyndham guided Q4 US RevPAR in line with Q3.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: 2026-08-05: RevPAR/EBITDA guide raised but EPS guide trimmed, stock +2.93%. 2025-11-05: guide cut, stock +5.98% (bar was low). 2026-04-30: EPS miss with a steady outlook, -15.58%. The direction of EPS guidance against the bar decides the large moves.
findings.why_not_priced: This is the bar itself, so it is priced by definition. The finding is the asymmetry: the raise the Street expects has to clear $7.14 on EPS, not only on RevPAR. If the market were relaxed about the EPS line, the whisper would sit at or above consensus. It sits $0.03 below.
findings.independence: Hilton's Q4 caution (midterms, Middle East), 2026-10-27: https://www.travelpulse.com/news/hotels-and-resorts/hilton-worldwide-reports-third-quarter-2026-earnings-results. Pointing the other way: Wyndham said Q4 US RevPAR would be in line with Q3's +6%: https://www.hoteldive.com/news/wyndham-earnings-q3-2026/833706/

findings.finding: This peer group sold its Q3 RevPAR beats. Wyndham printed US RevPAR +6% and raised its FY RevPAR guide after the close on 2026-10-21, then fell 4.2% (78.36 to 75.07) on Oct 22 and 3.5% on Oct 23, with adj EPS down 2% on a marketing-fund timing swing. Hilton printed US +7% and raised its RevPAR guide on 2026-10-27, and fell about 5% premarket on a revenue miss. CHH fell 1.5% and 3.1% in sympathy on Oct 22-23 (113.66 to 108.48), then recovered to about $112.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: CHH's own record: +2.93% on an RevPAR acceleration and raise (Aug 2026) and -15.58% on an EPS miss (Apr 2026). EPS quality, not RevPAR, has driven the large moves.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly in the price already: CHH gave back about half its run-up after WH's print and has recovered since. This finding is about the reaction function, not the fact. A strong US RevPAR number alone has not been rewarded in this group this season, so a CHH RevPAR beat without a clean EPS beat and raise may be sold too.
findings.independence: Hilton reaction (Reuters via TravelPulse, -5% premarket on a revenue miss despite a RevPAR raise): https://www.travelpulse.com/news/hotels-and-resorts/hilton-worldwide-reports-third-quarter-2026-earnings-results. CHH daily closes: https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/CHH?range=1mo&interval=1d

findings.finding: Crowded short into the print: 6.33M shares short (2026-10-15 settlement), 12.8 days to cover against roughly 0.49M average daily volume, about 14% of shares outstanding and more of the family-reduced float. If the US RevPAR and guidance raise the peers point to arrive with a clean EPS beat, short covering is a mechanism for an outsized upside move.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Two of the last seven reactions were +5.98% and +2.93% on raised or better-than-feared outlooks. The baseline does not record short interest at those dates.
findings.why_not_priced: Short interest is public, but 12.8 days to cover means the position cannot exit quickly. If shorts had covered on the WH/HLT read-through, short interest would have fallen sharply from the 6.6M at the 2026-07-15 settlement. It barely moved (6.6M to 6.33M).

findings.finding: The Q3 2025 comparison includes about $9.5M of liquidated damages (in other revenue) that will not recur, roughly $0.15 of adj EPS after tax on about 45M shares. Consensus $2.26 still asks for about +8% growth over last year's $2.10.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Not separately observable. The item was flagged by the company on the Q2 call.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced. The company guided to it explicitly, so it sits inside what the market was told to expect. It is filed because a sell-side model that missed it would make consensus slightly too high.

findings.finding: CEO Dominic Dragisich sold 1,227 shares at $112 on 2026-10-20 under a Rule 10b5-1 plan adopted 2026-02-24, leaving 90,055 shares held directly. The sale is small and pre-planned.
findings.why_not_priced: Public Form 4. The plan dates from before Q3 began, so it carries no information about the quarter.

findings.finding: On 2026-08-28 CHH signed a $500M senior unsecured term loan (SOFR+1.25%, maturing 2029-08-28, Wells Fargo agent) for general purposes including debt repayment. Net leverage was 3.1x at Q2, inside the 3-4x target, and the 2026 buyback is guided at $175-225M ($133M done by July 31). This is refinancing and capital-return capacity, not distress.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None observed. Higher interest expense was one reason the EPS guide was trimmed on 2026-08-05.
findings.why_not_priced: Public 8-K and mostly priced. What the money buys is refinancing plus buyback capacity at an investment-grade spread. A Q4 buyback acceleration would be a small positive.

outside_window.finding: The first disposition of wholly owned hotels (19 operating) is expected in H1 2027, subject to market conditions. It is a capital-recycling catalyst, but not in this window unless announced with the print.

baseline_tension: The evidence leans mildly with the +8.5% run-up (peer RevPAR strength, crowded short). It cuts against the peer group's sell-the-news reaction and a Street bar already above guidance. With no usable skew, there is no option-market direction to beat.
lessons_applied: Lesson 1 (verified fact is not a predicted reaction): RevPAR read-through cut from +0.8 to +0.7, p_up from 54 to 53, because the peer group sold its RevPAR beats and CHH's big moves turn on EPS and guidance.
Lesson 7 (crowded short shrinks negatives): reaction-function finding cut from -1.0 to -0.7 and Street-above-guide finding from -0.5 to -0.4, given 12.8 days to cover.
Lesson 4 (financing is a question): term loan kept at +0.1 after confirming it funds refinancing and buybacks at 3.1x leverage.
Lesson 6 (verify the bar): bar sourced to the company guide plus two agreeing EPS estimates ($2.26 / $2.28), so no cap applied.
'What has worked' (a peer print after the company last spoke) kept the read-through positive rather than zero.
